import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.21

by V. D. Mazurov

G. Higman proved that, for any prime number $p$, there exists a natural number
$\chi(p)$ such that the nilpotency class of any finite group $G$ having an
automorphism of order $p$ without non-trivial fixed points does not exceed
$\chi(p)$. At the same time he showed that $\chi(p) \geq (p^2 - 1)/4$ for any
such *Higman's function* $\chi$. Find the best possible Higman's function. Is it
the function defined by equalities $\chi(p) = (p^2 - 1)/4$ for $p > 2$ and
$\chi(2) = 1$? This is known to be true for $p \leq 7$.

Here "best possible" means pointwise least on the primes. Such a least Higman
function exists, since Higman functions are closed under pointwise minimum.
A finite group with a fixed-point-free automorphism of prime order is
nilpotent by Thompson's theorem; the formalisation asserts nilpotency
together with the bound on the nilpotency class.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.21»

/--
A function $\chi$ (on the primes) is a *Higman function* if, for every prime
$p$, every finite group $G$ having an automorphism of order $p$ without
non-trivial fixed points is nilpotent of nilpotency class at most $\chi(p)$.
The values of $\chi$ at non-primes are irrelevant.
-/
def IsHigmanFunction (χ : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (φ : MulAut G),
    orderOf φ = p → MonoidHom.FixedPointFree φ →
      ∃ _ : Group.IsNilpotent G, Group.nilpotencyClass G ≤ χ p

/--
The candidate for the best possible Higman function: $\chi(p) = (p^2 - 1)/4$
for $p > 2$ and $\chi(2) = 1$. (For odd $p$ the number $(p^2 - 1)/4$ is an
integer.)
-/
def higmanCandidate (p : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if p = 2 then 1 else (p ^ 2 - 1) / 4

/--
Find the best possible Higman's function. Is it the function defined by
equalities $\chi(p) = (p^2 - 1)/4$ for $p > 2$ and $\chi(2) = 1$?

That is, is the function `higmanCandidate` a Higman function which is
pointwise (on the primes) at most every other Higman function?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.21» : answer(sorry) ↔
    IsHigmanFunction higmanCandidate ∧
      ∀ χ : ℕ → ℕ, IsHigmanFunction χ → ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → higmanCandidate p ≤ χ p := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.21»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.21

by V. D. Mazurov

$\chi(p)$ such that the nilpotency class of any finite group $G$ having an
automorphism of order $p$ without non-trivial fixed points does not exceed
$\chi(p)$. At the same time he showed that $\chi(p) \geq (p^2 - 1)/4$ for any
such *Higman's function* $\chi$. Find the best possible Higman's function. Is it
the function defined by equalities $\chi(p) = (p^2 - 1)/4$ for $p > 2$ and
$\chi(2) = 1$? This is known to be true for $p \leq 7$.

Such a group $G$ is nilpotent by Thompson's theorem, so a Higman function is
formalised as a bound on the nilpotency class together with the assertion that
$G$ is nilpotent.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.21»

/--
A function $\chi$ on the primes is a *Higman function* if, for every prime $p$,
every finite group $G$ having an automorphism of order $p$ without non-trivial
fixed points is nilpotent of nilpotency class at most $\chi(p)$.
-/
def IsHigmanFunction (χ : Nat.Primes → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (p : Nat.Primes) (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (φ : MulAut G),
    orderOf φ = p → (∀ g : G, φ g = g → g = 1) →
      ∃ _ : Group.IsNilpotent G, Group.nilpotencyClass G ≤ χ p

/--
The *best possible* Higman function: a Higman function $\chi$ such that
$\chi(p) \leq \chi'(p)$ for every prime $p$ and every Higman function $\chi'$.
-/
def IsBestHigmanFunction (χ : Nat.Primes → ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsHigmanFunction χ ∧
    ∀ χ' : Nat.Primes → ℕ, IsHigmanFunction χ' → ∀ p : Nat.Primes, χ p ≤ χ' p

/--
The candidate Higman function of the problem: $\chi(p) = (p^2 - 1)/4$ for $p > 2$
and $\chi(2) = 1$. For an odd prime $p$ the number $p^2 - 1$ is divisible by $4$,
so the division is exact.
-/
def higmanCandidate (p : Nat.Primes) : ℕ :=
  if (p : ℕ) = 2 then 1 else ((p : ℕ) ^ 2 - 1) / 4

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem higmanCandidate_two : higmanCandidate ⟨2, Nat.prime_two⟩ = 1 := by
  decide

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem higmanCandidate_three : higmanCandidate ⟨3, Nat.prime_three⟩ = 2 := by
  decide

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem higmanCandidate_seven : higmanCandidate ⟨7, by norm_num⟩ = 12 := by
  decide

/-- Any function pointwise at least a Higman function is again a Higman function. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsHigmanFunction.mono {χ χ' : Nat.Primes → ℕ} (h : IsHigmanFunction χ)
    (hle : χ ≤ χ') : IsHigmanFunction χ' := by
  intro p G _ _ φ hφ hfix
  obtain ⟨hG, hc⟩ := h p G φ hφ hfix
  exact ⟨hG, hc.trans (hle p)⟩

/--
Is the best possible Higman function the function defined by
$\chi(p) = (p^2 - 1)/4$ for $p > 2$ and $\chi(2) = 1$?

That is, is every finite group having an automorphism of prime order $p$ without
non-trivial fixed points nilpotent of class at most $\chi(p)$, and does every Higman
function $\chi'$ satisfy $\chi(p) \leq \chi'(p)$ for every prime $p$? This is known to
be true for $p \leq 7$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.21» : answer(sorry) ↔ IsBestHigmanFunction higmanCandidate := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.21»

/-- Any two best possible Higman's functions agree at every prime. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBestHigmanFunction.apply_eq_of_prime {χ χ' : ℕ → ℕ} (hχ : IsBestHigmanFunction χ)

  obtain ⟨_, hle⟩ := hχ p hp G φ hφ hfree
  exact ⟨‹_›, hle.trans (h p hp)⟩

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.21

by V. D. Mazurov

G. Higman proved that, for any prime number $p$, there exists a natural number $\chi(p)$
such that the nilpotency class of any finite group $G$ having an automorphism of order $p$
without non-trivial fixed points does not exceed $\chi(p)$. At the same time he showed that
$\chi(p) \geq (p^2 - 1)/4$ for any such *Higman's function* $\chi$. Find the best possible
Higman's function. Is it the function defined by equalities $\chi(p) = (p^2 - 1)/4$ for
$p > 2$ and $\chi(2) = 1$? This is known to be true for $p \leq 7$.

Here a finite group with a fixed-point-free automorphism of prime order is nilpotent by
Thompson's theorem, so the nilpotency class in the definition of a Higman function is
well defined; the formalisation asserts the nilpotency explicitly.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.21»

/--
A function $\chi$ from the prime numbers to the natural numbers is a *Higman function* if
for every prime $p$, every finite group $G$ having an automorphism of order $p$ without
non-trivial fixed points is nilpotent of nilpotency class at most $\chi(p)$.
-/
def IsHigmanFunction (χ : Nat.Primes → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ᵉ (p : Nat.Primes) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G) (φ : MulAut G),
    orderOf φ = p → (∀ g : G, φ g = g → g = 1) →
    ∃ _ : Group.IsNilpotent G, Group.nilpotencyClass G ≤ χ p

/--
The candidate for the best possible Higman function: $\chi(p) = (p^2 - 1)/4$ for $p > 2$
and $\chi(2) = 1$. Note that $(p^2 - 1)/4$ is an integer for every odd prime $p$.
-/
def higmanCandidate (p : Nat.Primes) : ℕ :=
  if 2 < (p : ℕ) then ((p : ℕ) ^ 2 - 1) / 4 else 1

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem higmanCandidate_two : higmanCandidate ⟨2, Nat.prime_two⟩ = 1 := by
  simp [higmanCandidate]

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem higmanCandidate_three : higmanCandidate ⟨3, Nat.prime_three⟩ = 2 := by
  simp [higmanCandidate]

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem higmanCandidate_seven : higmanCandidate ⟨7, by norm_num⟩ = 12 := by
  simp [higmanCandidate]

/--
Is the best possible Higman function the one defined by $\chi(p) = (p^2 - 1)/4$ for $p > 2$
and $\chi(2) = 1$?

That is, is this function a Higman function, and does it bound every Higman function from
below (so that it is the pointwise least Higman function)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.21» : answer(sorry) ↔
    IsHigmanFunction higmanCandidate ∧
      ∀ χ : Nat.Primes → ℕ, IsHigmanFunction χ → ∀ p, higmanCandidate p ≤ χ p := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.21»

This is equivalent to the table's suggestion that the sharp function h(p) = sup of classes equals the candidate (Higman functions are closed under pointwise min, so the least one is h), while avoiding sSup-on-ℕ default-value pitfalls.
